milestones.label: Jacobi's note 'on decomposing a number into four squares'
milestones.work: C. G. J. Jacobi, Note sur la decomposition d'un nombre donne en quatre carres, J. reine angew. Math. 3 (1828) 191
milestones.description: The earliest title found that names the four-squares decomposition theme; it appears in Crelle's Journal a year before the 1829 Fundamenta nova.

evidence.claim: zbMATH record 'Note sur la decomposition d'un nombre donne en quatre carres', Jacobi, J. reine angew. Math. 3 (1828) 191
Crossref/DOI record for the same 1828 article (DOI from the zbMATH links)

milestones.note: Title-level naming of the theme, not a coinage of the modern name 'Jacobi's four-square theorem'. It predates the 1829 first_statement already in the record, so the conceptual derived date would move to 1828 if the content of the note confirms the four-square result. The note itself was not read. A reviewer should decide this.

works.citation: J. W. L. Glaisher, On the representation of an uneven number as a sum of four squares and as the sum of a square and two triangular numbers, Phil. Mag. (5) 1 (1876) 44-49
works.whyItMatters: A separate later analysis of four-square representations, for odd numbers, in the line opened by Jacobi's theorem.

works.citation: J. W. L. Glaisher, On the representations of a number as a sum of four squares, and on some allied arithmetical functions, Quart. J. Math. 36 (1904) 305-358
works.whyItMatters: A long systematic study of four-square representation numbers and related functions, following Jacobi's formula.
